audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill/Skill/Skill/Neeko/Skill/Neeko/Neeko while every 'why' line said Sett wins levels 2 onward.
audit.why: The mirror (neeko__sett) set both layers to the packet order — Neeko, then Sett for every later row — and a 55.43% win rate over 920 games backs it.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set to Neeko / Sett x6 as matched full+content pairs with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level-6 spike said to 'leap on her' and that R 'cancels' Pop Blossom's channel.
audit.why: The Show Stopper is a 400-range grab with no leap, on 120/100/80s. Pop Blossom is a leap (dash) with a preparation — R's grounding is what denies it. Riot's text says nothing about interrupting a channel, so 'cancel' is an unsupported word.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] and whys[4] now state the grounding denial and the 400-range limit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neeko referred to as 'he' in the TL;DR and dos; Facebreaker described as a pin that always stuns; Tangle-Barbs had no numbers.
audit.why: Neeko is female. Facebreaker stuns only when it catches enemies on opposite sides of Sett. Tangle-Barbs is 1000 range on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and grows larger, faster and longer-rooting after it passes through a champion — so a minion-line cast is more dangerous, not less.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed; mid now states the both-sides rule and the real Tangle-Barbs numbers.

audit.why: 12s at rank 1 is the whole engage window in this lane.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries range, cooldown and the pass-through growth.

edits.before: He kites your hands — hold W for his commit and E-stun the moment he steps to poke. Sett wins by trading around Neeko's Tangle-Barbs and cashing the pattern: bank grit, land the E-stun, cash the W panel.
edits.after: She kites your hands — hold W for her commit and E-stun the moment she steps to poke. Sett wins by trading around Neeko's Tangle-Barbs and cashing the pattern: bank grit, land the E-stun, cash the W panel.

edits.after: She kites your hands — hold W for her commit and E-stun the moment she steps to poke.

edits.before: E-stun him when Tangle-Barbs is down
edits.after: E-stun her when Tangle-Barbs is down

edits.before: Sett wins Level 6 because R cancels her Pop Blossom and punishes her channel.
edits.after: Sett wins Level 6: The Show Stopper grounds Pop Blossom's leap out of the fight.

edits.before: R The Show Stopper hard-counters her R Pop Blossom: leap on her the instant she channels the airborne windup and slam her, or use it to cancel her escape after she blows tantrum root.
edits.after: The Show Stopper (400 range, 120s at rank 1) grounds — grab her during Pop Blossom's preparation and the leap never happens. It is an answer, not a gap-close, so hold it for her step-up.

edits.before: From Level 2 onward the lane swings to you. E Facebreaker pins her, Q Knuckle Down closes the gap, and Haymaker's true-damage tail plus Grit sustain shrug off her poke. Her main out is E Tangle-Barbs root — dodge it and she has no way to survive your all-in. R cancels her Pop Blossom.
edits.after: From Level 2 onward the lane swings to you. Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides, so pull her across your wave, then cash Haymaker's true-damage centre. Tangle-Barbs is 1000 range on 12s and grows after passing a champion — dodge it and her all-in dies with it.

edits.before: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs: matchup-defining — Her root — extends through targets. Dodge it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs (E, 1000 range, 12s at rank 1): her root grows after passing a champion. Sidestep it, then commit.
